lines.say: Simon's Quest came out in Japan in 1987, and in America in December 1988.
You play as Simon Belmont again, hunting for five pieces of Dracula to break a curse.
The first game was a straight line. This one is an open world, with towns, shops, and leveling up.
Hearts aren't just pickups here. They're money, and you spend them in the town shops.
It has a day and night cycle. When night falls, the game stops to tell you:
What a horrible night to have a curse.

args.text: WHAT A HORRIBLE NIGHT TO HAVE A CURSE.

lines.say: At night, monsters get stronger, and the townspeople lock their doors.
And when morning comes, you get another message: the morning sun has vanquished the horrible night.

args.text: THE MORNING SUN HAS VANQUISHED THE HORRIBLE NIGHT.

lines.say: The villagers give you hints, but a lot of those hints are lies.
The manual even warns you that people don't always tell the truth.
One puzzle is legendary. Kneel by a cliff, holding a red crystal, and wait for a tornado to carry you away.
There are three endings, and which one you get depends on how fast you finish.
Its mix of exploring and leveling up came back years later, in Symphony of the Night.
Today, that style of game has a name: Metroidvania.
Did you ever figure out that cliff? Follow for more 8-Bit Backstory!
